done.why: I walked into the lake with my lantern and it got wet, and now it 'will not light again.' Every death put me back at the Endless Stair with only the dead lamp. The Junction just south is pitch black, so each time I tried to go anywhere a grue ate me. The sword, vial, hood, cloak and amulet were all lost. Restart is refused. I couldn't get any further, so I left.

about: A last test set by an old, ageless man who waits for you to prove you're worthy. You climb down into a shadowy land at the bottom of an endless stair and pass strange trials. You fight a hooded double of yourself and then spare it. You greet a ghostly sailor and he gives you a gift. You dive into a freezing lake for a gold amulet. Being clever and strong isn't enough here. It seems to be about judgment, mercy, and what you're willing to give up.

moments.note: 'Who do you think you are? Arthur?' when I tried to pull the sword out of the rock. Then the rock description, 'invited many times', made me grin.
The sword from the junction suddenly appeared in my hand, glowing, when the hooded figure showed up.
I took the hood off my beaten opponent instead of killing it and found my own face under it. Good payoff for holding back.
'hello sailor' actually worked, and he threw me a gift.
Lots of exits are just walls of flavor text ('Not today'). Beach north, wall north, northwest slide, east rubble, and west mist all closed off.
Getting into the lake made me drop everything, with no warning beforehand. Underwater I couldn't hold any of it ('drops from your grasp').
'take all' underwater answered 'There is no fish visible now.'
Got the shiny object and it turned out to be a golden amulet that I was suddenly wearing.
The Foggy Room was dark when I came back without a light, and a grue ate me. Then the prison-cell vision of the old man before waking at the stair.
The lamp 'will not light again'. One move into the lake ruined my only light, and from then on every route meant death in the dark.
Third grue death. It's a dead end that I can't restart.

wished: To dry out or fix the lantern, or find some other light
Some warning before the lake took everything I was carrying
A way to get my sword and vial back from the lake bottom
To restart after it was clear the game couldn't be won
To get past the many 'not today' exits (the beach path north, the wall, the rockslide)
To reach the south and west shores of the lake

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: Funny, and it told me the sword wasn't meant to come out yet.

lines.line: The rock has the look of a thing that has been invited many times.
lines.why: Dry and lovely prose, much better than a plain description.

lines.line: You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: The best moment of the game. Sparing the figure paid off.

lines.line: I have waited three ages for someone to say those words and save me from sailing this endless ocean.
lines.why: It rewarded a silly guess and it was charming.

lines.line: It has the look of an old friend who has followed you somewhere it would rather not have come. ... it will not light again.
lines.why: Touching, and also the moment I knew my game was over.

lines.line: I await you, though your journey be long and full of peril. Go then, and let me not wait long!
lines.why: The death scene repeats the goal: find the old man.

fun.why: The duel, the sailor and the amulet were real highs. Then one mistake at the lake left me with no light, no items and no restart, and the last stretch was just repeated grue deaths.

engagement.why: The goal was clear from the opening dream, and each discovery pulled me on until I got stuck.

difficulty.why: Losing the lamp is permanent and there was no warning. Combined with dark rooms, being reset to the stair, and no restart, one easy mistake ended the game for good.

interestingness.why: Puzzles about mercy and self-knowledge (unmasking my double, greeting the sailor) felt meaningful. A lot of the map was walled off with 'not today' text, though.

prose.why: The new descriptions (the rock, the lamp, the blocked paths) are witty and full of mood. Some odd answers like the fish line broke it a little.
